name: 20th Naval Construction Battalion
plain: a naval construction battalion (Seabees), about a thousand men who built airstrips, roads and bases, followed from Nouméa through the Solomons and New Guinea to Okinawa
note: Seabees. Formed at the Naval Construction Training Center, Norfolk, August 1942. Sailed in two waves, from San Francisco on 6 Oct and from San Pedro on 29 Nov 1942 (ncbhist-020/p10-p11), and reunited at Nouméa on 13 Dec 1942. In May-June 1943 it split: a Forward Echelon of about 500 men (the 1st Section) went to Townsville, Woodlark and Kiriwina with the Seventh Fleet; the Rear Echelon (the 2nd Section; its rolls are headed "Detachment" in Sep 1943 and "Second Section" from Dec 1943) went by Guadalcanal and the Russells to New Georgia with the Third Fleet. Reunited on Banika, Russell Islands, 6 Jun 1944; home in September 1944; Saipan and Okinawa in 1945 (in two echelons, April and May); broken up there on 29 Aug 1945, its men transferred to the 15th, 36th, 79th and 126th Battalions (ncbhist-020/p2-p3; rg24-190273312/p0835). Its 1942 rolls number the sections the other way round: the roll headed "Sec 2" in Oct 1942 is the first wave, forwarded from Nouméa, while "Section 1" was still at Port Hueneme.

relations.note: The half that sailed from Port Hueneme on 6 Oct 1942 (the rolls' "Sec 2"); reunited with the second wave at Nouméa on 13 Dec 1942 (ncbhist-020/p2).
The half that stayed at Port Hueneme until 26 Nov 1942 (the rolls' "Section 1") (ncbhist-020/p2).
About 500 men: Townsville, Woodlark, Kiriwina, Milne Bay, Brisbane; the 1st Section from October 1943 (ncbhist-020/p2-p3).
The rest: Guadalcanal, the Russells, New Georgia, then Banika; the 2nd Section, its rolls headed "Detachment" and "Second Section" (ncbhist-020/p2-p3).

About 400 men (12 officers, 403 men; 1 1/2 companies) under Lt. Riordan at Oloana Bay, Vangunu (ncbhist-020/p2, p11; mcsol ch. 2). Its first echelon (3 officers, 114 men) left for Bau Island on 9 September 1943, its second (10 officers, 262 men) for Ondonga on 9 and 15 October (ncbhist-020/p11-p12). (split from Rear Echelon)

About 140 men (3 officers, 142 men; one company) under Lt. Sanders at Viru Harbor (ncbhist-020/p2, p11); left in echelons on 5-9 September 1943 for East Rovianna and Doke Doke, and from East Rovianna for Bau Island, arriving 5 November (ncbhist-020/p11-p12). (split from Rear Echelon)

The PT-boat base on Bau Island, Rendova Harbor: Group One's first echelon from 10 September 1943, joined by the Viru company on 5 November; 4 officers and 211 men left for the Russells on 9 January 1944 (ncbhist-020/p11-p12). (split from Rear Echelon)
23 officers and 749 men, Saipan to Okinawa in four LSTs, 12-17 April 1945 (ncbhist-020/p12; LST-824 and LST-898 war diaries).
4 officers and 276-277 men, on Saipan until 7 May 1945; joined the first echelon on Okinawa on 14 May (ncbhist-020/p12, p5).

name: Convoy No. 91
plain: a four-ship Takao–Hong Kong convoy, known mostly from a secondary source
note: Attacked southwest of Pratas Island (東沙島) on 4 July 1944; the diary estimated two or three submarines. SEAHORSE's attacks pair with Kuri's two sinking reports by time and place; BANG's with Kuri's 0515 "no damage" report by time alone (inferred). **Ports, cargo and the number of ships are not recorded** in the 2nd China Expeditionary Fleet diary. "To Hong Kong" is inferred from the course on SEAHORSE's attack sheets (270, then 320–335) and the escorts, which were Hong Kong's (Kuri and Hatsukari escort another convoy off 碣石湾 on 29 July, p26). SEAHORSE counted five freighters and two destroyers with other escorts.
